facts.statement: Schizorhiza possessed a robust snout featuring more than 1,800 denticles arranged in dense rows to create a continuous cutting edge on both sides.
facts.quote: Schizorhiza is characterized by its robust rostrum with over 1,800 denticles arranged in dense batteries, which form a continuous cutting edge along each side.

facts.statement: The denticles on Schizorhiza's snout were replaced by smaller nested denticles within their roots while new rows grew from the tip of the snout.
facts.quote: Each denticle was replaced by a series of smaller denticles nested inside its roots and new rows of denticles grew from the end of the rostrum.

facts.statement: The species Schizorhiza stromeri was first described by Wilhelm Weiler in 1930 based on rostral denticles found in the Nubian Sandstone of Egypt.
facts.quote: Schizorhiza stromeri was named by Wilhelm Weiler in 1930 for rostral denticles from the Nubian Sandstone of Egypt.

facts.statement: A second species, S. weileri, was named by Giselda Serra in 1933 based on rostral denticles discovered in Libya.
facts.quote: A second species, S. weileri, was named by Giselda Serra in 1933 for rostral denticles from Libya.

facts.statement: The species S. weileri is currently considered a junior synonym of S. stromeri.
facts.quote: It is considered a junior synonym of S. stromeri.

facts.statement: Schizorhiza lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages and its fossils have been found in Africa, the Middle East, North America, and South America.
facts.quote: It lived from the Campanian to Maastrichtian, and its fossils have been found in Africa, the Middle East, North America, and South America.

facts.statement: Schizorhiza lived between 83.6 and 66 million years ago during the Campanian to Maastrichtian periods.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Schizorhiza belongs to the family Sclerorhynchidae.
Schizorhiza is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.

rejected.quote: The rostrum was likely used for swiping and slicing prey like sawfishes and has earned Schizorhiza the common name of 'slasher ray'.
